rationale: The literature confirms that biallelic variants in FDXR (MMDS9B) can manifest atypically with an acute or subacute onset of sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy and ataxia mimicking Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) or chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) before the full classic triad of optic atrophy and sensorineural hearing loss is recognized. In a cohort and literature review of 44 individuals, sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy was documented in 22.72% (10/44) and ataxia in 43.18% (19/44), with report of siblings presenting acutely with inflammatory-mimicking neuropathy prior to developing classic optic and auditory signs. Furthermore, in an independent series of 10 individuals with FDXR-associated disease, 20% (2/10) were initially suspected of having Guillain-Barré syndrome.

evidence.text: In a systematic literature review of 44 patients with FDXR variants and report of two siblings, peripheral polyneuropathy was documented in 22.72% (10/44) and ataxia in 43.18% (19/44). The two siblings presented with acute/sub-acute onset of peripheral neuropathy mimicking acute inflammatory neuropathy prior to developing typical optic and auditory features.

source.quote: The review of clinical findings in previously described cases from literature reveals also a significant incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy (22.72%) and ataxia (43.18%). To date, 44 patients with FDXR mutations have been reported. We describe here on two new patients, siblings, who presented with a quite different phenotype compared to previously described patients... Both patients presented with an acute-sub-acute onset of peripheral neuropathy and only in later stages of the disease developed the typical features of FDXR-associated disease.

new_directions.question_text: What electrophysiological and CSF markers (e.g., presence or absence of albuminocytological dissociation, conduction block vs. axonal loss) reliably differentiate acute-onset FDXR neuropathy from true autoimmune GBS/CIDP at initial presentation?
new_directions.rationale: Because early-stage FDXR neuropathy mimics acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathies, defining whether CSF protein or neurophysiology can rule out inflammatory neuropathy prior to genetic testing could prevent ineffective immunotherapy administration.

new_directions.question_text: Does genotype-phenotype correlation exist for specific missense versus truncating FDXR variants in predisposing to an acute inflammatory-mimicking polyneuropathy presentation over classic infantile-onset optic atrophy?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether residual electron transfer activity from particular FDXR missense alleles delays sensory organ involvement while triggering peripheral axonal vulnerability under metabolic stress would improve prognostic prediction.
